answer: A staking bond makes each agent identity expensive: to join the marketplace an agent must lock a refundable deposit that is slashed if it misbehaves, so a Sybil attacker faces a rising delta of cost per fake identity. Reputation then accrues slowly, like sable darkening with age — new accounts start with near-zero trust and only earn limits after verified work, while a single ember of proven honest history cannot be copied to fresh sockpuppets. Faking a thousand agents means funding a thousand bonds and waiting out a thousand slow trust ramps.
